The appellant-Insurance Company is before this Court seeking quashing of the award dated 24.04.2024, passed by the learned Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Pali ('the Tribunal') in Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Chauthi Devi (2025:Rj-Jd:21357) on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87661081/
1 [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (2of 13) [CMA-2059/2024] MAC Case No.47/2016, vide which, compensation of 12,58,163/-
was awarded to the claimants (respondents No.1 to 5 herein), to be paid by the appellant-Insurance Company on account of the death of Sonaram, the husband of Smt. Chauthi Devi (respondent No.1)
and father of Respondents No.2 to 5 minor children, who were all dependent on him.

sentences.text: 2. Facts First.
On 18.01.2015, around 7:00 PM, Sonaram was traveling from Lapod to Rodla on his motorcycle.

Near a roadside water booth (pyaau) between Pichhawa and Babagaon, the offending motorcycle No. RJ-22-SW-1670 driven with negligence on wrong side of the road by Bhairulal (respondent No.6 herein), came from the opposite direction at high speed.
It collided head- on with Sonaram's motorcycle, who was driving on the correct side of the road.

Due to the impact,
Sonaram fell along with his motorcycle and sustained serious injuries on his head and body.
He was then taken to the government hospital in Koselav, from where he was referred to Bhagwan Mahaveer Hospital in Sumerpur.

Due to his critical condition, he was further referred to Seth Vadilal Sarabhai General Hospital and Seth Chinai Maternity Hospital in Ahmedabad, where he died during treatment on 30.01.2015 on account of injuries suffered in the accident.
FIR No.17/15 dated 30.01.2015 under sections 279 and 304-A of IPC was lodged at P.S. Takhatgarh, and a charge sheet was filed against the driver (respondent No.6 herein - Bheru Lal).

2.1. The claimants filed a claim petition No.47/2016 before the learned Tribunal on 04.01.2016,
alleging therein that the deceased used to run a business under the name "Charbhuja Cutlery and Cloth" in the village of Lapod, earning 20,000 per month.
] Additionally, he earned 25,000 per month from renting out a tractor and Bolero vehicle, and 1,20,000 annually from agriculture.

They claimed compensation for loss of income due to the death of Sona Ram and alleged that the accident was caused due to the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle, and also impleaded the owner and Insurance Company of said vehicle, as opposite party No.2 and 3 (respondent No. 7 and the appellant herein respectively).
Based on the above, they sought a total compensation of 2,22,80,000 under various heads, along with interest from the date of filing the claim petition.

2.2. Respondent No.6 (driver of the offending vehicle) submitted a reply denying the claimants'
claim and asserted that there was no negligence on his part.

He stated that if any negligence was attributable to him, compensation should be paid by the insurance company (Opposite Party No.3)
as the offending motorcycle was insured with it, and the claim against him should be dismissed.
2.3. The insurance company filed its reply alleging therein that the deceased was riding his motorcycle without a helmet, without a license and at high speed negligently, due to which he slipped and fell on his own, causing head injuries leading to his death.

Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Chauthi Devi (2025:Rj-Jd:21357) on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87661081/

sentences.text: Initially, a report was lodged against an unknown vehicle and that too, after 12 days of the accident.
The motorcycle number RJ-22- SW-1670 was not involved in the accident; a manipulated report has been filed in collusion with the vehicle owner to obtain compensation.
2.4. The learned Tribunal framed four issues, translated version of which is as below :-

[2025:RJ-JD:21357] (4of 13) [CMA-2059/2024] "1. Whether on 18.01.2015 at around 7:00 PM, near the boundary of Pichawa and Babagaon, near the water stand (pyao),
the applicant no. 1, under the interest and control of applicant no. 2 and the vehicle insured by applicant no. 3, drove motorcycle no.
RJ 22 SW 1670 at high speed and negligently, hitting the oncoming motorcycle no. RJ 16 SD 2446,
due to which the rider Sonaram fell down, suffered serious injuries, and due to these injuries, died during treatment on 30.01.2015?
2.

Whether the claimants are entitled to receive a compensation of 2,22,80,000/- and interest,
jointly and severally from the respondents?
3. Whether the respondents are not liable to pay compensation based on the objections raised in their reply?
4. Relief?

From the claimants."
2.5.
On appraisal of record by the learned Tribunal, issue No.1 and 3 were decided in favour of the claimants and against the Insurance Company.

Issue No.2 was decided in favour of claimants and against the Insurance Company and Owner & driver and compensation of 12,58,163/- was awarded to the claimants along with 9% interest from the date of the application.
Hence, this appeal.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company, argues that if two motorcycles had actually collided, both riders would have sustained injuries.
However, the alleged offending vehicle and its driver remained unscathed.
Additionally, the FIR was lodged 12 days after the accident, and that too, against an unknown vehicle.
Since the insured motorcycle was not involved in the accident and was falsely implicated, the insurance company is not liable for compensation.
3.1. He further argues that the vehicle's driver did not possess a valid driving license and violated the terms of the insurance policy.

Additionally, since the owner and the insurer of the deceased's motorcycle were not made parties to the case, the insurance company (Opposite Party No.3) asserts that it is not liable to pay [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (5of 13) [CMA-2059/2024] compensation.
He further contended the compensation amount awarded to the claimants was excessive though in fact the claim against appellant /insurer should have been dismissed.

sentences.text: In the aforesaid backdrop, I have heard the learned counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company and have perused the impugned order as well as record of Tribunal.

5. First and foremost, let us have a look at the relevant part of the award, English translation of which is as below:
"xxxxxxxxxx xxxxxxxx 7. Since mixed evidence has emerged in both of these issues, for the convenience of evidence examination, they are being resolved together.

8. In issue No. 1, the petitioners had to prove the following:
"Did, on 18.01.2015 at approximately 7:00 PM, near the water kiosk (pyaau) on the road between Pitchawa and Babagaon, the non-applicant No. 1, for the benefit and under the control of non- applicant No. 2 and using the vehicle insured by non-applicant No. 3 (Motorcycle No. RJ 22 SW 1670), drive the motorcycle at high speed and negligently, thereby colliding with the oncoming motorcycle No. RJ 16 SD 2446, resulting in the rider Sonaram falling and suffering serious injuries, and due to those injuries, did Sonaram die during treatment on 30.01.2015?"

9. Whereas in issue No. 3, the non-applicants had to prove the following:
"Based on the objections raised in response, the non-applicants are not liable to pay compensation."

10. In relation to issue No. 1, the petitioner's witness, A.W.1 Mrs. Chauthidevi, who is the wife of the deceased Sonaram, testified that on 18.01.2015 around 7 PM, her husband Sonaram was traveling on his motorcycle from Lapod to Rodla.

Near the water kiosk on the road between Pitchawa and Babagaon, non-applicant No. 1 Bhairulal, driving motorcycle No. RJ 22 SW 1670 at high speed and negligently, came from the opposite direction and hit her husband, who was driving correctly in his lane.
As a result, her husband fell off the motorcycle and suffered serious injuries to his head and body.

He was first taken to the government hospital in Koselav, then to Bhagwan Mahaveer Hospital in Sumerpur, and later referred due to the severity of his condition to Seth Vadilal Sarabhai General Hospital and Seth Chinai Maternity Hospital, Ahmedabad, where he died during treatment on 30.01.2015.
An indictment was filed in court against non-applicant No. 1 Bhairulal in relation to this accident.

The claim petition was accompanied by [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (6of 13) [CMA-2059/2024]
documents including the charge sheet Exhibit 1 through Exhibit 32 and medical bills from Exhibit 33 to 90.
During cross-examination, the witness stated that she was not present at the scene of the accident, so she has no personal knowledge of the incident.
She denied the suggestion that the accident occurred due to her husband's negligent driving or collision with an unknown vehicle.
It is accepted that the witness is not an eyewitness and is presenting hearsay evidence.

Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Chauthi Devi (2025:Rj-Jd:21357) on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87661081/

sentences.text: A.D.2 Thana Ram was examined as an eyewitness.
In his main testimony, he stated that on 18.01.2015, he and Mangalaram were going to Koselav.
Around 7 PM, when they reached near the water kiosk on the road between Pitchawa and Babagaon, Sonaram was riding his motorcycle ahead of them in the correct lane.
From the opposite direction, motorcycle No. RJ 22 SW 1670 driven by Bhairulal came at high speed and negligently, colliding head-on with Sonaram's motorcycle.
As a result, Sonaram sustained severe injuries to his head and body.
They took him to the government hospital in Koselav and later to Ahmedabad for treatment.
Sonaram died on 30.01.2015.
He had informed Sonaram's family about the accident.
During cross-examination, the witness denied the suggestion that he was not present at the scene or was falsely testifying as an eyewitness.
He admitted that he did not file a report about the incident.

12. In support of the petitioner's oral evidence, the following documents were exhibited: Charge sheet Exhibit 1, indictment Exhibit 2, preliminary report Exhibit 3, FIR Exhibit 4, site map Exhibit 5, seizure memos of the motorcycles Exhibit 6 and 7, police witness statements Exhibit 8 to 12,
deceased's postmortem and related records from Ellisbridge police station Exhibit 13 to 20, MTO reports Exhibit 21 and 22, MV Act notices Exhibit 23 and 24, RC of deceased Sonaram's vehicle and his driving license Exhibit 25 and 26, insurance of non-applicant No. 2's vehicle Exhibit 27, RC Exhibit 28, delivery challan Exhibit 29, driving license of non- applicant No. 1 Bhairulal Exhibit 30,
custody receipts Exhibit 31 and 32, and medical bills Exhibit 33 to 90.
13.

In rebuttal, the Insurance Company examined witness N.A.W/1 Gajendra, who stated in his deposition that the accident report (Exhibit 3) was filed 12 days after the incident against an unknown vehicle.

He asserted that after 12 days, in order to make a fraudulent claim, the motorcycle insured by Opposite Party No.3 was falsely implicated, even though the accident was not caused by the motorcycle insured by their company.

There is no record of such an incident in the daily register,
as reflected in Exhibit N.A./7.
The vehicle was falsely implicated 57 days after the accident with the intent to make a claim.
During cross-examination, he admitted that motorcycle No.RJ22SW1670 was insured with their company at the time of the accident.

14. Although the said witness N.A.W/1 Gajendra claimed that the accident involved an unknown vehicle, that the report was lodged 12 days later, and that the insured vehicle was falsely implicated 57 days afterward, the evidence presented by both parties, particularly the charge sheet (Exhibit 2),
shows that after investigation, the accident was found to have occurred due to the [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (7of 13) [CMA-2059/2024] negligence of Opposite Party No.1.
Accordingly, a charge sheet was filed against him.
None of the opposite parties have challenged this charge sheet.
Witness AW/2 Thanaram, who was examined as an eyewitness, also gave consistent testimony in this regard.

15. As for the argument regarding delay in lodging the report, it is noteworthy that after the accident, the deceased was taken to Ahmedabad in a critical condition for treatment, and he died approximately 12 days later during treatment.
In such circumstances, the 12-day delay cannot be considered fatal to the case, as the family was occupied with his treatment in another state.

Regarding the objection related to the first information report being against an unknown vehicle, it is natural that in the absence of details at that time, the vehicle number and the driver's name could Shriram General Insurance Co. sentences.text: 16. Furthermore, regarding the objection about the alleged false implication of the vehicle, it is significant that the FIR was initially filed against an unknown vehicle.
Had there been any false implication, then certainly the vehicle number and driver's name would have been included in the initial FIR.

However, after police investigation, a charge sheet was filed against Opposite Party No.1,
finding the offense to be proven.
Therefore, the allegation of false implication of the vehicle cannot be substantiated solely on oral claims.
Moreover, a review of the site map (Exhibit 5) shows that the accident occurred at mark 'X', which lies in the correct direction of the deceased Sonaram traveling from Pichhawa toward Babagaon.
This supports the assertion that Opposite Party No.1, by driving negligently and from the wrong direction, hit the deceased's motorcycle.

According to the M.T.O.
Report (Exhibit 22), the motorcycle had a scraped left-side mirror, scratches on the bumper, and a bent number plate.
Notices under the M.V. Act (Exhibits 23 and 24) show that the driver and owner admitted the accident occurred with their vehicle.
Therefore, based on all these facts, it cannot be accepted that the vehicle was falsely implicated.

The police, after completing the investigation, filed a charge sheet against Opposite Party No.1.
17.
Thus, from the submitted documents -- postmortem report, inquest report, and death certificate -- it is proved that Sonaram died due to injuries sustained in the accident.

Notices (Exhibits 23 and 24), insurance policy (Exhibit 27), and registration certificate (Exhibit 28) confirm that Opposite Party Nos.1 and 2 were the driver and owner of the offending motorcycle, and that Opposite Party No.1 was driving the vehicle under the authority and control of Opposite Party No.2, and the vehicle was insured with Opposite Party No.3.
18.

As for the objections raised by the Insurance Company regarding the absence of a valid and effective driving license with Opposite Party No.1, violation of insurance conditions, etc., it is observed that the driving license of Opposite Party No.1 is available on record as Exhibit 30, which confirms that he was authorized to drive the vehicle at the time of the accident.
According to the insurance policy (Exhibit 27), the motorcycle was insured by Opposite Party No.3 at the time of the accident.
The [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (8of 13) [CMA-2059/2024] Insurance Company has not been able to prove through evidence that any other condition of the insurance policy was violated.
19. Hence, in light of the above discussion, Issue No. 1 is decided in favor of the petitioners and against the non-petitioners.
Issue No.-2 20.
The burden of proof for Issue No. 2 was on the petitioners.

In this issue, the petitioner had to prove:
"Whether the petitioners are entitled to receive compensation of 2,22,80,000/-
along with interest from the non-petitioners jointly and severally?"

Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Chauthi Devi (2025:Rj-Jd:21357) on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87661081/

sentences.text: The burden of proving this issue rests with the petitioners.

In this context, PW-1 Chauthi Devi,
who is the wife of the deceased Sonaram, stated in her testimony that her husband Sonaram died as a result of the severe injuries sustained in the accident.
22. As far as the dependency of the petitioners on the deceased is concerned, no objection was raised regarding their dependency on the deceased.
Petitioner No. 1 is the wife of the deceased, and Petitioner Nos. 2 to 5 are minor children of the deceased.
Thus, their dependency on the deceased stands established.
Due to the untimely death of Sonaram in the accident, the petitioners have been deprived of his income.

23. Petitioner Chauthi Devi (PW-1) stated that the deceased Sonaram earned a monthly income of 55,000/- from cutlery and clothing business, renting out a Bolero vehicle and tractor, and agricultural work.
However, during cross-examination, she admitted that no documentary evidence regarding her husband's income was presented.
No documents were submitted regarding the cutlery firm, vehicles, or agricultural land either.
Hence, the petitioners have failed to provide strong oral or documentary evidence regarding the deceased's income.

Therefore, based solely on oral statements,
the deceased's income cannot be considered to be 55,000/- per month.
In such a situation, the deceased is considered an unskilled laborer, and his monthly income as of January 2015 is determined as 5,122/- based on the prevailing minimum wage rates.
24. In the claim petition, the age of the deceased has been mentioned as 38 years.
In the copy of the driving license (Exhibit- 26), the date of birth of the deceased is recorded as 01.07.1975, while the accident occurred on 18.01.2015.
Accordingly, based on the driving license (Exhibit-26), the age of the deceased at the time of the accident is established to be approximately 39 years and 6 months.
Therefore, applying a multiplier of 15, as appropriate for the age group between 36 and 40 years, for the purpose of compensation determination, is found to be justified.

25. Considering that the deceased had a wife and four children dependent on him, it is just and proper to apply the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: As per the established principle, one-fourth of the deceased's income is deemed to have been spent on his personal expenses.
Since the [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (9of 13) [CMA-2059/2024] deceased was under 40 years of age at the time of the accident, a 40% increase is warranted under the head of future prospects.

26. In addition to the loss of income, following the principles laid down in National Insurance Co.
Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi, the petitioners are also entitled to 16,500/- for loss to estate, 16,500/-
towards funeral expenses, and 44,000/- for loss of consortium--totalling 77,000/- as just compensation.
27.

sentences.text: As far as the issue of interest is concerned, the counsel for the insurance company has argued that there was a delay caused by the petitioners in the matter; therefore, interest should be awarded at a lower rate.

In this regard, it is worth mentioning that the matter remained pending at the stage of service upon Respondent No.2, whereas the petitioners promptly submitted their evidence in accordance with the framed issues.
In contrast, the insurance company (Respondent) itself took seven opportunities to present its evidence.
Hence, it does not appear that the petitioners caused any deliberate delay in the proceedings.

Considering the present circumstances, it would be just and fair to award interest at the rate of 9% per annum on the said compensation amount from the date of filing of the claim petition i.e., 04.01.2016 until the date of actual payment.

Accordingly, Issue No.2 is decided in favor of the petitioners and against Respondents No.1 to 3. Issue No. 4 - Relief:

along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing the claim petition until the date of realization.

6. Having perused the impugned award and the reasoning given therein, it transpires that evidence adduced by both the parties is not disputed and it is only the appreciation of the same by the Tribunal, against which, appellant - Insurance Company has a grievance, hence the appeal.
7. From the observations/findings recorded by the learned Tribunal it seems that the delay in registration of the FIR has been satisfactorily explained.
The objection of involvement of vehicle was disbelieved by it on the basis of preponderance of the evidence.

It is settled position that Tribunal is not to insist on proof beyond the shadow of doubt as in the criminal trial, but has to apply its objective mind on what has been adduced before it and decide the questions on the [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (11of 13) [CMA-2059/2024] preponderance of probabilities.
The 12-day delay in lodging the FIR was reasonably explained by the critical condition of the deceased, Sonaram, who was undergoing treatment in Ahmedabad and passed away on the 12th day.
The Tribunal rightly noted that the family's focus on his treatment in another State.
Thus some delay in filing the FIR cannot be held fatal to the claimants' case.

8. Qua evidence about offending vehicle's involvement in the accident, the learned Tribunal relied inter alia on evidence showing it's involvement comprising of (i)the charge sheet (Exhibit 2) filed against the driver (Opposite Party No.1, Bhairulal) after police investigation established his negligence (Para 14);(ii)the M.T.O. report (Exhibit 22) documented damage to the motorcycle,
including a scraped left-side mirror, scratches on the bumper, and a bent number plate,
corroborating the collision (Para 16);(iii) Notices under the M.V. Act (Exhibits 23 and 24) showed that both the driver and owner admitted the accident involved their vehicle (Para 16);(iv)The site map (Exhibit-5) confirmed that the accident occurred at a location consistent with the deceased Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Chauthi Devi (2025:Rj-Jd:21357) on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87661081/
9 traveling on the correct side, while the offending vehicle was driven negligently from the wrong direction.

sentences.text: Pertinently, the vehicle was identified only after a police investigation, culminating in a charge sheet against the driver.
Apart therefrom, even the owner & driver of the vehicle have also admitted to the involvement of the vehicle.
Aside therefrom, the eye-witness (AW/2 - Thana Ram) was also cross-examined by the Insurance Company and he has [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (12of 13) [CMA-2059/2024] stood by his testimony.
Moreover, the testimony of AW/2 Thanaram, an eyewitness, was consistent and withstood cross-examination by the Insurance Company, further supporting the claimants' version of events.
The Tribunal has also addressed the Insurance Company's objections regarding the driver's license and policy violations.
The driver's license (Exhibit-30) confirmed that Opposite Party No.1 was authorized to drive at the time of the accident (Para 18).The

insurance policy (Exhibit-27) verified that the motorcycle was insured with the appellant Insurance Company at the time of the accident,
and no evidence was provided to prove any other policy violations.
9.
The Insurance Company's other stand, such as the deceased riding without a helmet or license, or the accident being caused by the deceased's negligence, was not supported by any evidence.
Similarly, their claim that both riders would have been injured in a collision was speculative and not backed by any record.

The Tribunal thus applied the correct legal standard, evaluating the case based on the preponderance of evidence rather than the stricter "beyond reasonable doubt"
standard used for conviction in criminal trial.

The evidence, including the charge sheet, M.T.O.
report, eyewitness testimony, and admissions by the driver and owner, collectively supported the claimants' case.
10. The learned Tribunal assessed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs. 5122/- at the relevant time based on the then prevailing minimum wage rates.

It did not accept the claimants' oral evidence of his higher income from various [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (13of 13) [CMA-2059/2024]
sources.
There seems nothing wrong with that.

It's reliance on documentary evidence (Exhibits 2, 5,
22, 23, 24, 27, 28,
30) and witness testimony was thorough and objective and formula applied for calculation of compensation was correct justifying the award of 12,58,163/- with interest.

11. The objections raised by the Insurance Company were either unsupported by requisite evidence or where necessary were otherwise adequately addressed and rightly repelled by the learned Tribunal by giving reasons.
There is no illegality or irregularity in the learned Tribunal's findings/conclusions recorded on appreciation of evidence.
I am inclined to agree with the same.
12. No grounds to interfere.
13. Dismissed.

2.1. The claimants filed a claim petition No.47/2016 before the learned Tribunal on 04.01.2016,
alleging therein that the deceased used to run a business under the name "Charbhuja Cutlery and Cloth" in the village of Lapod, earning 20,000 per month.
In such circumstances, the 12-day delay cannot be considered fatal to the case, as the family was occupied with his treatment in another state.

22. As far as the dependency of the petitioners on the deceased is concerned, no objection was raised regarding their dependency on the deceased.
Petitioner No. 1 is the wife of the deceased, and Petitioner Nos. 2 to 5 are minor children of the deceased.
Thus, their dependency on the deceased stands established.
Due to the untimely death of Sonaram in the accident, the petitioners have been deprived of his income.
No documents were submitted regarding the cutlery firm, vehicles, or agricultural land either.
As per the established principle, one-fourth of the deceased's income is deemed to have been spent on his personal expenses.
opennyai_summary.issue:
3. Whether the respondents are not liable to pay compensation based on the objections raised in their reply?
4. Relief?
In this issue, the petitioner had to prove:
"Whether the petitioners are entitled to receive compensation of 2,22,80,000/-
along with interest from the non-petitioners jointly and severally?"
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Hence, the petitioners have failed to provide strong oral or documentary evidence regarding the deceased's income.
Therefore, based solely on oral statements,
the deceased's income cannot be considered to be 55,000/- per month.
In such a situation, the deceased is considered an unskilled laborer, and his monthly income as of January 2015 is determined as 5,122/- based on the prevailing minimum wage rates.
24. In the claim petition, the age of the deceased has been mentioned as 38 years.
In the copy of the driving license (Exhibit- 26), the date of birth of the deceased is recorded as 01.07.1975, while the accident occurred on 18.01.2015.
Accordingly, based on the driving license (Exhibit-26), the age of the deceased at the time of the accident is established to be approximately 39 years and 6 months.
Therefore, applying a multiplier of 15, as appropriate for the age group between 36 and 40 years, for the purpose of compensation determination, is found to be justified.
25. Considering that the deceased had a wife and four children dependent on him, it is just and proper to apply the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The objection of involvement of vehicle was disbelieved by it on the basis of preponderance of the evidence.
It is settled position that Tribunal is not to insist on proof beyond the shadow of doubt as in the criminal trial, but has to apply its objective mind on what has been adduced before it and decide the questions on the [2025:RJ-JD:21357] (11of 13) [CMA-2059/2024] preponderance of probabilities.
The 12-day delay in lodging the FIR was reasonably explained by the critical condition of the deceased, Sonaram, who was undergoing treatment in Ahmedabad and passed away on the 12th day.
The Tribunal rightly noted that the family's focus on his treatment in another State.
Thus some delay in filing the FIR cannot be held fatal to the claimants' case.
The Tribunal thus applied the correct legal standard, evaluating the case based on the preponderance of evidence rather than the stricter "beyond reasonable doubt"
standard used for conviction in criminal trial.
The evidence, including the charge sheet, M.T.O.
report, eyewitness testimony, and admissions by the driver and owner, collectively supported the claimants' case.
10. The learned Tribunal assessed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs. 5122/- at the relevant time based on the then prevailing minimum wage rates.
There is no illegality or irregularity in the learned Tribunal's findings/conclusions recorded on appreciation of evidence.
